x: The Velanati line ended when the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva killed its last member (C). Some notes name him Mummadi Rajendra Choda and add that Nellore Choda Tikkana helped Ganapatideva kill Prithvisvara; Mallavarma was the progenitor and Gonka I the founder, so A and D are wrong.
A Kota chief married Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva; some notes name him Bhimaraju II. This marriage reflects the Kotas becoming Kakatiya vassals.

Land tax exemptions were handled and granted through the ur, the village assembly of ordinary (non-brahmadeya) villages. The nagaram was a merchant body and the sabha was the Brahmin assembly of brahmadeya villages.

Rajendra I's 1025 CE naval expedition was against the revived Srivijaya empire: he defeated the Sailendra king and took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra. Anuradhapura was destroyed by Rajaraja I, and Kalinga was conquered by Kulottunga I.
Chola-Sailendra ties, once cordial, soured when Srivijaya blocked Indian traders on the China route; Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition cleared these obstacles and widened Chola trade with China.
The Pithapuram inscription of the Velanati Choda Prithvisvara names Kolleru Lake (APPSC 2017).
